newsitem.title: USA: San Diego finalizes sale of solid waste system.
newsitem.headline: San Diego finalizes sale of solid waste system.

text.p: An ambitious plan by San Diego County to sell its solid waste system has entered its final stage and should be completed in two weeks, county officials said on Tuesday.

San Diego County Chief Administrative Officer Lawrence Prior will recommend Wednesday a buyer for the system, which includes four landfills, a transfer station, a recycling plant and all county-owned and leased waste bin and container sites.
The three finalists are Allied Waste Industries Inc, USA Waste Services Inc and Waste Management Inc, county officials said.

Over the next two weeks county officials will negotiate final terms of the sale with the buyer recommended by Prior. The county Board of Supervisors is scheduled to vote on the terms on Aug 12, county officials said.
The privatization of a municipal asset of this size is unprecedented in California. San Diego County expects to take in between $125 million and $200 million from the sale.

The money raised will be used to retire outstanding county bonds and cover liabilities. Proceeds will also be used to establish an environmental trust fund for the maintenance of inactive landfills and to build up the county budget reserve.
